Subject: Hosted vs Reserved capacity: decision matrix and next steps

Hi Samir / Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a recommended next step so we can align on deployment mode (Hosted API vs Reserved GPU / Dedicated) for FastLedger's fraud-scoring feature.

Summary of signals from the call:
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end inference <= 120ms for user-facing scoring (bursty traffic around 150 qps peak).
- Sustained throughput: ~30 qps baseline, spikes to 150 qps for 2-5 minute windows during batch windows.
- Model: 13B retrained model; KV cache expected to reduce repeated context.
- Data sensitivity: PCI-adjacent, log retention policy required; customer prefers private routing but is open to hosted SSO if controls are present.

Attached: a lightweight decision matrix (rl-decision-matrix.xlsx) that maps latency/throughput combinations to our recommended deployment: Hosted for elastic, Reserved for predictable high-throughput low-latency, Private VPC for strict isolation. Also attaching our sample SLA (rw-sla-sample.pdf) for review.

Clarifying asks so we can finalize recommendation:
1) Can you confirm the typical request payload size (tokens) and the expected median/95th prompt length?
2) For the 150 qps spike, is concurrency single-request per user or many parallel user requests?
3) Any internal compliance requirement that makes on-prem/VPC mandatory (beyond log retention)?

Proposed next steps:
- Fast turn: we produce two configuration sketches (Hosted + autoscale settings; Reserved GPU pool sizing) and cost delta within 3 business days.
- Technical pilot: 2-week pilot on Reserved capacity if you want to validate p95 under representative load.
- If you want Private VPC, we'll include a deployment checklist and estimate.

If you can reply with answers to the three clarifying points, I’ll route to Rishi for an SLO/instance sizing sketch and Marissa for pricing.

Thanks — Naomi

Thanks Samir — helpful detail. Quick technical read on options with the numbers you provided: 

A) Hosted API (recommended if you prioritize time-to-value / variable cost):
- Pros: immediate scale during spikes with autoscaling; minimal ops overhead.
- Cons: may need aggressive concurrency control; expected p95 depends on instance mix and sustained cache hit rate.
- Sizing note: to target p95 <= 120ms at 150 qps for a 13B with typical 120 token prompts, we'd need a mix of optimized c4 instances with batching + KV cache and an autoscaler targeting 160% of steady state. Estimated cost: see attached Decision Matrix.

B) Reserved (Dedicated GPU pool):
- Pros: deterministic latency (lower variance), better unit cost at sustained volumes, more predictable cold-start behavior.
- Cons: commit required; less flexible for very spiky load unless you provision headroom or allow burst capacity.
- Sizing note: a small Reserved pool sized for peak concurrency will comfortably hold p95 <= 120ms; pilot recommended to validate end-to-end egress and network hops.

C) Private VPC/on-prem:
- Pros: full isolation for compliance; control plane in-region and KMS tie-ins.
- Cons: longer lead time and higher TCO.

My recommendation for FastLedger given the bursty but predictable peak windows: run a Reserved pool sized to handle the 150 qps peak for production scoring, and use Hosted as a fallback to absorb unexpected spikes while you ramp. That gives you p95 predictability while retaining elasticity.

If that sounds reasonable I’ll draft a pilot plan: 10-day baseline capture -> 2-week Reserved pilot (with load tests) -> production cutover checklist. Marissa can produce cost delta and contract term language.

— Rishi
